record_note: UnicodeChecker was wired to the kit on 2026-09-22 on branch process/plunk-in-the-gate, taking every artifact below from kit revision 9f3ff726 in one sitting (PLUNK-IN rung 5). CLAUDE.md is deliberately absent: the kit's rung-1 contract requires Harri's explicit approval and he was not present for this run, so no CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md was created and none is listed here. INCIDENTS.md is the one adapted file -- the kit's log verbatim plus this repo's own entries on top. The adopted_fixes[] block was added by the follow-up record-only commit named in adopted_in, because a commit cannot name itself. A draft agent contract sits in CLAUDE_PROPOSED.md for Harri to accept or reject; it is not listed here because nothing was copied for it -- if he adopts it as CLAUDE.md it becomes a files[] entry (templates/CLAUDE.md.template, adapted). **2026-10-06, hook-tier port:** adopted_fixes gains hook-tiers-agree and the record's revision moves to 919006e, the kit commit the two probes in tools/kit-probes/ are carried from verbatim — the convention's rule is that a revision that moves re-verifies the WHOLE copy, so every kit_sha256 here is re-read at that copy point, not just the new file. tools/ci.sh remains this repo's own adaptation of the template (see its adapted_why); the port added CI_FAST_STAGES/CI_FULL_STAGES and the `fast`/`full` arguments to it, and the pre-commit hook now names the tier. optimized-stage.sh had to be refreshed with the probe: its R5 read the CI_DEFAULT_STAGES line literally and would have failed on the unchanged list. **2026-10-06, card t_075c0a6f (KitCI fleet batch 2 of 3):** the gate is no longer a bash script. tools/ci.sh and the probes under tools/kit-probes/ are DELETED; the gate is the tracked gate.toml (11 stages, tiers fast/full) run by kit-ci, plus scripts/gate-env.sh, scripts/gate.sh and one scripts/<stage>.sh per stage — all of them this repo's own files, which is why none appears in files[] below. files[] loses tools/ci.sh and every tools/kit-probes/*.sh entry: the artifacts are gone, so no hash can describe them. The kit fixes those probes guarded move from adopted_fixes to declined_fixes — not because the fixes were declined, but because the artifact they CHECK no longer exists (each probe is written against a single bash gate file; measured against scripts/gate.sh, see INCIDENTS.md for the verdicts). The contracts did not go: each one has a named home, listed in INCIDENTS.md entry by entry. .githooks/pre-commit and .githooks/pre-push are RE-HASHED because this commit edits them: they now NAME a tier (--tier fast, and --tier full with CI_REQUIRE_CLEAN=1, the old --require-clean flag moved into the environment), and their branch for this repo's own tools/ci.sh is gone with that file. `revision` and every other entry are UNCHANGED: nothing here came from the kit, and being behind the kit is not a failure. **2026-10-07 (L3, card t_5d78dc03, Harri's mark-don't-mend ruling):** the files[] entries below were last accurate at revision 98e517d; the fleet moved to KitCI on 2026-10-07 (L3), and drift after that is unrecorded by policy. The record says so with `fingerprints_retired` instead of re-reading the stale hashes: .ci.env.example's `repo_sha256` is RETIRED (no longer verified against disk), and the `adapted_why` it had been missing since the conversion is supplied from the repair plan.

files.adapted_why: Adapted 2026-10-06 (card t_075c0a6f, the KitCI conversion): four edits, all of them re-pointing prose at the new gate. (1) the header's "default in tools/ci.sh" now reads "scripts/gate-env.sh"; (2) the `CI_DEFAULT_STAGES="tree format kitprobes build tests release version asan tsan tidy pristine"` line is replaced by the note that the stage LIST moved to gate.toml's tiers, that scripts/gate-env.sh still reads the three CI_*_STAGES variables but they no longer select the run, and that CI_STRICT_TOOLS has no equivalent; (3) `tools/ci.sh --write-tidy-baseline` -> `scripts/write-tidy-baseline.sh`; (4) "tidy_key in tools/ci.sh" -> "scripts/gate-env.sh". Measured: the diff against the kit blob at 98e517d is exactly these four hunks (15 changed lines). Byte-identical to FSMTable's copy of the same file.

the port gives the commit hook the fast tier's NAME instead of the kit's explicit stage list. The kit ships the explicit list on purpose; measured here it is the spelling that goes stale -- the 2026-09-22 incident in INCIDENTS.md is exactly that list falling a stage behind, and FSMTable's fast tier cost a pushed commit that clang-format would have rewritten. So: one list in tools/ci.sh, N callers naming a tier.

no stage list: the hook calls `tools/ci.sh --require-clean`, so a push runs whatever CI_DEFAULT_STAGES says. The kit ships an explicit list on purpose (so a stage cannot be silently dropped); measured here, the explicit list instead went STALE the moment a stage was added -- the push ran 11 of 12 stages and printed GATE PASSED. One definition, N callers.
